title: Cereal seed is not import-dependent: over 80% of wheat seed is farm-saved and certified seed adoption is below 20%. Vegetable seed imports were US$16 million in 2023; local variety loss is reported but unmeasured

rootCauses.cause: Certified cereal seed production is small (30,000 t in 2023) and run by a centralised public network (Office des Céréales, DGPA), with local actors marginal, so certified seed adoption stays below 20%

author: TahaGHZ

sections.heading: Problem
sections.content:
The brief described a dependence on imported certified seed, cereals included, and an erosion of local varieties. The evidence supports only part of that.

For **cereals**, seed is overwhelmingly domestic. More than 80% of wheat seed comes from farm-saved or informal channels. Certified seed adoption is below 20% nationally and below 30% even in irrigated or high-potential areas, under the FAO benchmark of 30% (SRC-TG-827). Certified cereal seed production was 30,000 t in 2023 (SRC-TG-827). The cereal problem is low use of certified seed, not import dependence. The country does import about 1.6 Mt of wheat grain a year (SRC-TG-827), which is a separate problem covered in FND-TG-700.

For **vegetables**, seed for sowing is imported: 372.6 t worth US$16.3 million in 2023, up from US$12.4 million in 2013 (SRC-TG-824). The share of needs this covers, and whether any vegetable seed is produced or exported domestically, is not known.

**Local varieties**: the national gene bank says traditional varieties have been abandoned in favour of improved commercial seed and is reintroducing them (SRC-TG-830). The 2024 national treaty report lists "l'appauvrissement de la palette de variétés cultivées" (the narrowing range of cultivated varieties) among the threats (SRC-TG-828). The same report admits that genetic erosion is not measured to standard criteria and lacks baselines (SRC-TG-828).

sections.heading: Root causes
sections.content:
- **Cereal seed system (current, institutional).** The wheat seed system is highly centralised around the Office des Céréales and the DGPA, with regional services, cooperatives and collectors on the margins. The paper argues this limits local adaptability and innovation adoption (SRC-TG-827); the low certified-seed adoption figure is consistent with that diagnosis but is not shown to result from centralisation alone.
- **Seed law (context, effect unproven).** Law 99-42 of 10 May 1999 (JORT no. 39, 14 May 1999, p. 706) replaced the 1976 law. It created an official catalogue for varieties that are distinct, stable, uniform and of significant cultivation value (art. 4), and allows only seed of catalogued varieties to be marketed (art. 9) (SRC-TG-829). Its effect on local varieties is not established in the sources opened.
- **Reported variety replacement (low confidence).** The gene bank reports that traditional varieties have been abandoned in favour of improved commercial seed, while noting that some local varieties yield less (SRC-TG-830). The treaty report's Deglet Nour example is about date palms and belongs to the dates-and-oases finding, not cereal or vegetable seed (SRC-TG-828; see FND-TG-740).
- **Vegetable seed imports.** Imports are recorded (SRC-TG-824), but the export query returned no record, which counts as missing data rather than zero. Why vegetable seed is imported (breeding capacity, F1 hybrids, plant breeders' rights) was not documented.

sections.heading: Evidence
sections.content:
- Wheat seed adoption, farm-saved share and certified production: SRC-TG-827 (peer-reviewed; the figures are cited from DGPA 2024).
- Vegetable seed imports in 2013 and 2023: SRC-TG-824.
- Legal framework: SRC-TG-829 (law 99-42, JORT scan) and SRC-TG-828 (2024 treaty report listing 99-42 and its decrees 2000-101, 2000-102 and 2000-1282).
- Gene bank activity and its statements on variety loss: SRC-TG-830 (press, tier C).
- Qualitative threats and missing erosion baselines: SRC-TG-828.

sections.heading: Why confidence is what it is
sections.content: Medium for the cereal part: one recent peer-reviewed paper, relaying DGPA figures, gives consistent numbers (below 20% adoption, over 80% farm-saved). Vegetable seed import values come from UN Comtrade, a tier A dataset, but the dependence share is unknown. The loss of local varieties rests on qualitative official statements, one tier B report and one tier C press article, and is low confidence. The link from the seed law to erosion is not established.

sections.heading: Links to other sectors
sections.content: Water: the gene bank head says local varieties withstand climate shocks better than some imported varieties, which need more water, fertiliser and pesticides (SRC-TG-830). This is the official's claim, not measured data. Energy: none found.

sections.heading: Leads for phase 2
sections.content:
- National cereal extension programme with INGC aimed at improving farm-saved wheat seed quality (SRC-TG-827).
- Subsidies for certified cereal seed prices and strategic cereal seed reserves under the Office des Céréales, recommended by FAO (SRC-TG-820): https://www.fao.org/3/cc6217fr/cc6217fr.pdf
- Contracts with cereal growers for certified seed multiplication (SRC-TG-820).
- BNG on-farm conservation programmes, started with 200 producers and now covering more than 300 ha, and the repatriation of about 6,000 samples (SRC-TG-830).
- National gene bank database (www.tn-grin.nat.tn) (SRC-TG-828).
- Digital platforms and participatory governance for the wheat seed system (SRC-TG-827).

sections.heading: Verification
sections.content:
Seed-system, trade, gene-bank and legal figures were checked against the cited sources.

**Independent review, 21 November 2026:** pass. Checked in the originals: Gharbi 2026 (Frontiers, SRC-TG-827) abstract, introduction para. 2 and section 3.3; UN Comtrade HS 120991 imports for 2023 and 2013 (SRC-TG-824); La Presse 18 Nov 2026 on the gene bank (SRC-TG-830; the sentence on lower yields of some local varieties was confirmed in the saved transcript only, not in the live page fetch); Law 99-42 (SRC-TG-829) JORT header and arts. 1, 4, 9, 50; TIRPAA 2024 report (SRC-TG-828) art. 5 question 6, p.5. No corrections. Independent teammate sign-off is outstanding; reviewer and author share the TahaGHZ identity, so the record is not validated.

resolvedSources.title: Le système agricole et agroalimentaire tunisien face aux crises: focus sur la chaîne de valeur céréalière - Constats et réflexions pour la proposition d'un plan de relance à court et à moyen termes
resolvedSources.publisher: FAO (Chebbi, H.E., Amrani, M. et Bouallegui, F.), Tunis
resolvedSources.extracts:
Section 6.2, p. 42:

> La Tunisie connait depuis quelques années des difficultés à couvrir ses besoins en engrais pour le bon déroulement des saisons agricoles. Annuellement, ces besoins sont estimés pour les principaux engrais chimiques à près de 45 000 tonnes pour le triple super phosphate (TSP, super 45 pour cent), à près de 200 000 tonnes pour l'ammonitrate agricole – 33,5 pour cent – et à près de 90 000 tonnes pour le di-ammonium phosphate (DAP)69.

> 69 Selon un communique de presse du ministre en charge de l'agriculture en 2021.

English gloss: For some years Tunisia has struggled to cover its fertiliser needs. Annual needs are estimated at about 45,000 t TSP, 200,000 t agricultural ammonium nitrate (33.5%) and 90,000 t DAP (figures from a 2021 press release of the agriculture minister).

p. 43:

> Pour la campagne céréalière 2020-2021, la consommation tunisienne d'engrais a baissé à seulement 9 000 tonnes de super 45 pour cent, à 153 000 tonnes pour l'ammonitrate et à 71 000 tonnes pour le DAP.

English gloss: In the 2020-21 cereal season, fertiliser consumption fell to only 9,000 t TSP, 153,000 t ammonium nitrate and 71,000 t DAP.

Figure 25, p. 43, title and ammonium nitrate data labels (thousand tonnes, seasons 2010-2011 to 2020-2021 in order), as read from the text layer:

> figure 25. Évolution des quantités d'engrais utilisées en céréaliculture (1 000 tonnes)

> 152 188 176 214 196 194 181 187 190 157 153

English gloss: Fertiliser used in cereal growing. Ammonium nitrate on cereals: 152 kt (2010-11), 188, 176, 214, 196, 194, 181, 187, 190, 157 and 153 kt (2020-21).

p. 43:

> Force est de rappeler que le Groupe chimique tunisien (GCT) traverse depuis quelques années de grandes difficultés pour poursuivre sa production des engrais phosphatés destinés essentiellement au marché national, notamment l'ammonitrate agricole et le di-ammonium phosphate70. En 2020, le manque des engrais sur le marché intérieur, a contraint les autorités en place à importer, via le GCT, 60 000 tonnes d'ammonitrate, principalement de la Fédération de Russie. Ces achats d'un montant de 45 MDT sont destinés principalement à couvrir les besoins des grandes cultures.

English gloss: GCT has for some years had great difficulty keeping up production of fertilisers intended mainly for the domestic market, notably ammonium nitrate and DAP. In 2020 the domestic shortage forced the authorities to import, via GCT, 60,000 t of ammonium nitrate, mainly from Russia, worth 45 million dinars, mainly for field crops.

p. 43:

> Les frictions au niveau de l'offre d'engrais sur le marché national et certaines spéculations au niveau des circuits de distribution ont aussi continué à être observées en 202171. Cette baisse de l'offre de production tunisienne à cause des tensions sociales et des blocages au niveau des sites de production a coïncidé avec le resserrement du marché mondial des engrais de 2021 [...]

English gloss: Supply frictions and some speculation in distribution channels continued in 2021. The fall in Tunisian output, due to social tensions and blockades at production sites, coincided with the 2021 tightening of the world fertiliser market.

Footnotes 70-71, p. 43:

> 70 Avant la crise sociale post-2011 du secteur minier, l'industrie tunisienne arrivait à valoriser près de 85 pour cent de la production nationale de phosphate naturel. Ainsi, le GCT pouvait traiter annuellement près de 6,5 millions de tonnes de phosphate naturel, au niveau de ses quatre sites de production (Gabès, Sfax, Skhira et M'dhilla) [...]
> 71 Certaines sources estiment que la production tunisienne n'a pu couvrir que 25 pour cent de la demande intérieure d'engrais en 2021.

English gloss: Before the post-2011 social crisis in mining, Tunisian industry processed about 85% of national phosphate rock output; GCT could process about 6.5 Mt a year at four sites (Gabès, Sfax, Skhira, M'dhilla). Some sources estimate domestic production covered only 25% of domestic fertiliser demand in 2021.

p. 44:

> En Tunisie, même si le gouvernement est toujours intervenu directement et indirectement pour subventionner les prix des engrais et les maintenir à des niveaux inférieurs aux prix internationaux73, la hausse importante enregistrée des prix entre 2020 et 2021 sur le marché national a atteint 11 pour cent pour le super 45 pour cent et le DAP et près de 28 pour cent pour l'ammonitrate agricole [...]

> 73 À titre d'exemple des interventions étatiques sur le marché tunisien des engrais, le Ministère en charge du commerce a fixé, en décembre 2020, les prix de vente de l'ammonitrate à la production (430 dinars/tonne), les marges de distribution (25 dinars/tonne au gros et 45 dinars/tonne au détail) et le prix de vente aux agriculteurs (500 dinars/tonne).

English gloss: The government has always intervened directly and indirectly to subsidise fertiliser prices and keep them below international prices; still, domestic prices rose 11% for TSP and DAP and about 28% for ammonium nitrate between 2020 and 2021. Example: in December 2020 the commerce ministry fixed the ex-factory price of ammonium nitrate (430 TND/t), distribution margins (25 TND/t wholesale, 45 TND/t retail) and the farm-gate price (500 TND/t).

p. 61:

> Constat: problème d'accès aux engrais à temps et absence de stock de régulation des engrais

English gloss: Finding: problem of timely access to fertilisers and no fertiliser buffer stock.

p. 61 to 62, recommendations:

> • Des campagnes de vulgarisation devraient être mises en place pour éviter la surconsommation et le gaspillage des engrais pour une meilleure valorisation des quantités disponibles.

> • Faciliter l'accès (les achats) et l'utilisation des engrais dans un contexte de hausse des prix sur le marché international par la mise en place de mécanismes de crédits et de garanties pour les achats d'intrants;
> • Constituer des stocks de réserves pour assurer la disponibilité des engrais en quantité et en temps opportun:

English gloss: Extension campaigns to avoid over-use and waste of fertiliser; credit and guarantee mechanisms for input purchases; reserve stocks to ensure fertiliser is available in time.

p. 62, seed recommendations:

> · consolidation du programme de subventions des prix des semences céréalières sélectionnées (et certifiées);
> · promouvoir l'engagement des céréaliculteurs moyennant des contrats de multiplication des semences certifiées;
> · consolidation du programme d'approvisionnement en semences sélectionnées (et certifiées);
> · instaurer un programme de subventions pour la constitution de stock des réserves stratégiques de semences céréalières sous l'égide de l'OC;

English gloss: Strengthen subsidies on selected and certified cereal seed prices; promote multiplication contracts with cereal growers; strengthen certified seed supply; subsidise strategic cereal seed reserves under the Office des Céréales.
resolvedSources.notes: FAO-published study by named authors; views are the authors'. Fertiliser "need" figures come from a ministerial press release; SRC-TG-836 shows they are the quantities programmed for the 2020/21 season. The consumption series (figure 25, built from DGEDA and ONAGRI data) covers cereals only, not all crops. The figure 25 ammonium nitrate labels are legible in the text layer (series ordered from 2010-11 to 2020-21, one value per season); DAP and TSP labels and figure 27 values are less clearly ordered and are not used. The 25% coverage figure is attributed only to "certaines sources" and is weak. The statement that GCT fertilisers are "destinés essentiellement au marché national" should be read against UN Comtrade data showing large DAP exports (SRC-TG-824).

resolvedSources.title: Social network analysis of Tunisia's wheat seed system: from centralized structures to inclusive and adaptive governance
resolvedSources.publisher: Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems 10:1729520 (Gharbi I., Ouerghemmi H., Dhraief M.Z., Toukabri W., Ferchichi N., Oueslati M., Bahri H., Frija A., Annabi M.; INRAT and ICARDA)
resolvedSources.extracts:
Section 1, Introduction:

> In 2023, certified cereal seed production totaled 30,000 tons (24,000 tons durum, 3,800 tons bread wheat), yet adoption remained below 20% nationally and 30% in irrigated areas or high-potential areas, well below the FAO's recommended benchmark of 30%. Over 80% of seeds are sourced from farm-saved or informal channels, highlighting the need to expand certified seed production and strength farmer-oriented extension services. This low adoption rate reflects multiple structural and functional constraints within the WSS (Hammami and Gharbi, 2018; Direction Générale de la Production Agricole, 2024).

> Despite its strategic importance, Tunisia produces only a fraction of its wheat demand, importing nearly 1.6 million tons annually, exposing the country to price volatility and geopolitical risk (Thabet et al., 2024).

Section 3.3:

> A national cereal extension program, implemented with INGC, targets farmsaved wheat seeds, which account for roughly 80% of total wheat seed use, improving quality toward certified standards and strengthening seed security.

Abstract:

> Results reveal a highly centralized network dominated by public institutions, notably the Cereals Office and the General Directorate of Agricultural Production. While centralization ensures national coherence and strategic coordination, it limits local adaptability, inclusiveness, and innovation adoption. Territorial actors, including agricultural services, farmers' organizations, cooperatives, and seed collectors and distributors, occupy marginal positions, weakening feedback loops essential for responsive decision-making and context-adapted seed dissemination.

> The enhancement of the performance of the wheat seed system necessitates the implementation of formalized participatory governance, the consolidation of the capacities of local actors, and the integration of digital platforms to optimize the flow of information and enable the provision of timely feedback.
resolvedSources.notes: Peer-reviewed, open access (CC BY), published 16 February 2026. The adoption and production figures are cited from DGPA (2024) and earlier work, not measured by the study itself; the study's own data are 25 semi-structured interviews.

> Loi nº 99-42 relative aux semences, plants et obtentions végétales. Cette loi fixe les modalités de production, de multiplication, d'importation, de commercialisation des plants, des semences et des obtentions végétales ainsi les modalités de protection des droits s'y rapportants.

> · Décret nº 2000-1282, fixant la forme du catalogue officiel, les procédures d'inscription des variétés végétales et les conditions d'inscription des semences et plants obtenus récemment sur la liste d'attente. 2000-06-13
> · Décret nº 2000-101, fixant la classification des semences et plants, leur production et multiplication, les normes générales de leur stockage, emballage et étiquetage, le contrôle de leur qualité et état sanitaire et leur commercialisation. 2000-01-18

English gloss: Law 99-42 on seeds, plants and plant varieties sets the rules for production, multiplication, import and marketing of seeds and plants and for protecting related rights.

Article 5, question 6, p. 5:

> La diversité biologique en Tunisie est confrontée à plusieurs menaces naturelles ou anthropiques. Les menaces de nature anthropique, qui pèsent lourd sur la diversité biologique, englobe l'urbanisation, l'appauvrissement de la palette de variétés cultivées, l'intensification des cultures et les utilisations non rationnelles de pesticides, la dégradation des espaces steppiques et des forêts, etc.

English gloss: Human threats to biodiversity include urbanisation, the narrowing of the range of cultivated varieties, crop intensification, irrational pesticide use, and degradation of steppe and forest.

p. 5:

> L'évaluation de l'érosion génétique n'est pas souvent standardisée selon des critères internationaux et souffre d'un manque d'informations sur les états initiaux ;

English gloss: Assessment of genetic erosion is often not standardised to international criteria and lacks baseline information.

p. 6 (oases):

> Dans les oasis de Kébili, la dominance de la variété Deglet Nour rend une majorité des variétés communes de datte en situation menacée et sont de plus en plus rares.

English gloss: In the Kebili oases, the dominance of Deglet Nour puts most common date varieties under threat; they are increasingly rare.

Article 9 (farmers' rights), question 19B, p. 13: the field asking for details of measures taken to protect farmers' rights, including the right to save, use, exchange and sell farm-saved seed, is left empty (">>>" with no text).
resolvedSources.notes: Official country report submitted 19 November 2024 through the Treaty's online system; qualitative, no quantified erosion indicators. Classified tier B because it is a self-reported questionnaire, not statistics.

resolvedSources.title: Loi n° 99-42 du 10 mai 1999, relative aux semences, plants et obtentions végétales (JORT n° 39 du 14 mai 1999, p. 706 et suivantes)
resolvedSources.publisher: Journal Officiel de la République Tunisienne (scan hosted by FAOLEX)
resolvedSources.extracts:
Page header of the scan:

> Page 706 Journal Officiel de la Republique Tunisienne - 14 mai 1999 NO 39

Article 1:

> La presente loi s'applique a toutes les semences, plants et obtentions vegetales utilises dans la production vegetale.

Article 3:

> Les semences et plants de toutes les especes et varietes de plantes agricoles sont classes dans les categories suivantes: - semences et plants de base - semences et plants certifies - semences et plants standards

Article 4:

> II est cree un catalogue officiel sur lequel seront inscrites les varietes vegetales, elles sont distinctes, stables, homogenes et a valeur culturale importante.

Article 9:

> Ne peuvent etre commercialises que les semences et plants des varietes vegetales inscrites au catalogue officiel dans l'une des categories visees a l'article 3 de la presente loi.

Article 15:

> L'autorite competente assure la protection des obtentions vegetales lorsque ses obtenteurs ou leurs ayants droit Ie demandent.

Article 50:

> La loi n° 76-113 du 25 novembre 1976 relative a l'organisation, au controle de la production et de la commercialisation des semences et plants est abrogee.

English gloss: The law covers all seeds, plants and plant varieties used in crop production; classifies seed as basic, certified or standard; creates an official catalogue of varieties that are distinct, stable, uniform and of significant cultivation value; allows only seed of catalogued varieties to be marketed (art. 9); protects plant varieties at the request of their breeders (art. 15); and repeals law 76-113 of 1976.
resolvedSources.notes: Typeset JORT pages, scanned and OCR'd by FAOLEX. The OCR text contains errors ("sernences", "cornpetente", "II" for "Il"); extracts above correct only obvious OCR letter swaps and drop accents as in the OCR, and should be checked against the JORT image or legislation.tn (legislation.tn returned HTTP 503 on 2026-11-21; iort.gov.tn answered but was not searched for this text). Type "official-statistics" is used for lack of a "legal-text" type in the template.

resolvedSources.title: Semences locales : la Tunisie veut rapatrier 6 000 échantillons végétaux
resolvedSources.extracts:
Article published 2026-11-18, quoting the director general of the Banque Nationale des Gènes (BNG):

> La Banque Nationale des Gènes (BNG) de Tunisie a collecté et conservé 25 000 échantillons de ressources génétiques d'intérêt agricole, économique, médical et environnemental depuis le lancement effectif de ses activités en 2007, a annoncé son directeur général, Mohamed Ali Ben Tmessek.

English gloss: The BNG has collected and conserved 25,000 samples of genetic resources since it effectively started work in 2007.

> Selon le directeur général, les variétés locales et autochtones, adaptées à l'environnement tunisien depuis des millénaires, résistent nettement mieux aux aléas climatiques que certaines variétés importées, plus gourmandes en eau, en engrais et en pesticides.

English gloss: According to the director general, local varieties withstand climate shocks much better than some imported varieties, which need more water, fertiliser and pesticides.

> Dans cette optique, la BNG œuvre, en partenariat avec les centres de recherche scientifique et les agriculteurs, à la multiplication et à la réintroduction de variétés traditionnelles délaissées au profit des semences commerciales améliorées.

English gloss: The BNG works with research centres and farmers to multiply and reintroduce traditional varieties abandoned in favour of improved commercial seed.

> Mohamed Ali Ben Temessek a indiqué que 7 754 échantillons ont déjà été récupérés entre 2009 et 2021 auprès de banques de gènes étrangères, notamment en Australie, aux États-Unis, au Mexique et en République tchèque.

English gloss: 7,754 samples were repatriated from foreign gene banks (Australia, USA, Mexico, Czech Republic) between 2009 and 2021.

> Un plan est actuellement en cours pour récupérer quelque 6 000 échantillons supplémentaires à l'étranger, en donnant la priorité au henné, à la mloukhia (corète potagère), à la grenade, à la pastèque, ainsi qu'aux plantes médicinales et pastorales.

English gloss: A plan is under way to recover about 6,000 more samples from abroad, prioritising henna, mloukhia (jute mallow), pomegranate, watermelon, and medicinal and pastoral plants.

> Lancés avec 200 producteurs, les programmes de conservation à la ferme couvrent aujourd'hui plus de 300 hectares.

English gloss: Started with 200 producers, on-farm conservation programmes now cover more than 300 hectares.
resolvedSources.notes: Press report of statements by the BNG head; tier C. The claim about imported varieties' higher water and input needs is the official's assertion, not data. The article does not quantify how much area or how many varieties have been lost.

relatedItems.title: Tunisia imports more than half of its cereals (about 60% on ITES averages) and almost all of its soft (bread) wheat, even in good harvest years
Rainfed cereal output swings with rainfall and collapsed in the 2023 drought, cutting the harvest by roughly two-thirds or more

Irrigated fresh tomatoes, watermelons and citrus are grown almost entirely for the home market (about 2.4-4.1% exported in 2022), and agricultural policy as assessed by the World Bank in 2014 was biased against exports, so export promotion is not the main driver of their water use
